candidates.label: Disseminated trichosporonosis (Trichosporon asahii) with hepatosplenic abscesses, complicating neutropenia and acute promyelocytic leukemia
Hepatosplenic candidiasis (chronic disseminated candidiasis) due to echinocandin-resistant Candida species, in the setting of neutropenia and acute promyelocytic leukemia
Invasive aspergillosis with dissemination to liver and spleen and fungemia, in a neutropenic patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia
Disseminated fusariosis (Fusarium species) with fungemia and visceral involvement, in a neutropenic patient with acute promyelocytic leukemia
Disseminated coccidioidomycosis with hepatosplenic involvement, in an immunocompromised host with acute promyelocytic leukemia

response.rationale: The combination of yeast in blood cultures, arthroconidia and hyphal fungi on Gram stain, and high micafungin MIC with low voriconazole MIC strongly favors Trichosporon species, which is a known cause of disseminated infection in neutropenic patients. The hepatosplenic lesions and fever are consistent. Candidiasis is less likely due to the atypical Gram stain morphology and echinocandin resistance pattern. Aspergillosis and fusariosis are less consistent with yeast in blood cultures and arthroconidia. Coccidioidomycosis is unlikely given the absence of endemic exposure and the yeast form in blood.
